{"states":{"A":{"revision":4,"status":"queued"},"B":{"revision":3,"status":"cancelled"},"C":{"revision":1,"status":"ready"}},"eligible":["C"],"applied":7,"ignored":[{"event":"e4","reason":"stale"},{"event":"e3","reason":"duplicate"}]}

I can't adopt the official key's value here. Under the stated rules it is unreachable: at e3, R4 pushes A's *current* status ("queued") onto A's history stack before setting status to "blocked", so the stack is ["queued"]. At e6, R5 pops the most recent entry and restores A to "queued" (revision 4) — a revert never pushes "blocked", so "blocked" can never be popped. A restores to "blocked" only if the push happened after the status change, which contradicts R4. If you want A to end at "blocked", the rule text for R4/R5 must change (e.g. push the new status instead of the current one); with the rules and events unchanged, "queued" is the correct result.
